item.title: ‘What a joke’ – Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany calls out NFL’s bias against Chiefs after Bills loss
item.description: Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/NWSL via Getty Images Brittany Mahomes didn’t mince her words about the NFL’s officiating after the Kansas City Chiefs’ Thanksgiving Day defeat. The Buffalo Bills walked away with a 13-10 win over Super Bowl favourites Kansas City Chiefs in a closely contested 2026 Thanksgiving Day clash. However, the Bills’ win came with a plethora of criticism for the NFL from the Chiefs fanbase, including star QB Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany. The 31-year-old expressed her frustration over the highly debated overturned call in the fourth quarter. Brittany Mahomes lashes out at NFL officiating The moment that caught Brittany’s attention was an overturned catch by Rashee Rice in the fourth quarter of the Thanksgiving Day defeat. Mahomes called out the controversial decision in one of her Instagram stories, highlighted by NFL insider Ari Meirov on X . “HAHAHAHAHAHA WHAT A JOKE. Guess we can’t even play football without getting it called against us… not sure what an actual catch is after that, I guess? I don’t wanna hear s___ anymore from anyone,” Mahomes wrote. Considering the overturned play ultimately turned into a game-winning field goal at the buzzer for the Bills, Mahomes’ frustration is understandable. In fact, most NFL fans on social media resonated with the former soccer star’s sentiments and felt that the Chiefs were robbed of a clear catch. Following the three-point defeat, the Chiefs have now fallen to an 8-3 record, while the Bills are now 10-1 and look the outright favourites to win the Super Bowl this season. item.title: Poole's 100-game Pompey adventure
item.description: [Shutterstock] [BBC] In the summer of 2023 free agent Regan Poole turned down a higher salary elsewhere in League One to sign for Portsmouth. He did so believing the move to the south coast presented him with the best opportunity of reaching the Championship and furthering his career. Exactly 100 appearances later, he's been proved correct. Just like Poole's entire career trajectory, his time at Portsmouth has had plenty of ups and downs. After an excellent start and an international debut for Wales, he tore his anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee during an FA Cup defeat at Chesterfield. When he returned, Pompey were struggling to adjust to life in the Championship and the transition wasn't straightforward for Poole. Not helped by having to play many games in quick succession following a serious injury. Poole and Pompey improved and maintained their Championship status. Portsmouth spent, by their standards, significant fees on centre-backs Hayden Matthews and Josh Knight. Neither have looked like dislodging Poole. Even this season Poole struggled at the start, affected by injury and then below Benji Arthur and Conor Shaughnessy in the pecking order. He's fought his way back into the side and now looks every inch the Championship centre-back he was hoping to become. Portsmouth fans always appreciate committed players. Fratton Park is a ground where big tackles get a louder cheers than great pieces of skills. Poole puts his body on the line the way the home fans crave to see. He wears his heart on his sleeve, celebrating great tackles and blocks. He's absolutely buzzing after wins and often has a face of thunder after defeats (although he will front up to the media). Likely in a similar way to fans leaving the ground. Supporters also love to go on a journey with a player. Poole has grown and improved with the team in the nearly three and half years he's been here. His journey through football has been fascinating , making his Newport County debut at just 16 before moving to Manchester United and then fighting his way back up through the EFL. He's now going into the final year of his contract and has made it clear he would love to sign a new one . The club retain an option year in his deal so it seems very unlikely he'll be departing anytime soon. I highly doubt John Mousinho and Richard Hughes mentioned the Premier League when trying to sell the club to Poole. It would still require something miraculous for Pompey to reach the top flight imminently. But the fact I'm even mentioning it highlights what an adventure the first 100 Pompey matches have been for Regan Poole. item.title: US Merchant Marine Academy looking to make more history in Division III football playoffs
item.description: They’re sea-sing the day at the United States Merchant Marine Academy. It’s a historic year for the 8-1 Mariners, who will play in the second round of the Division III football playoffs for the first time in Kings Point history. “It’s really a special team and how close-knit they are,” head coach Jameson Croall told The Post. “Really, when times get difficult … we lean on each other and respond to that adversity together.” A U.S. Merchant Marine Academy player runs up field during his team’s 42-14 blowout win over the Coast Guard Academy on Nov. 14, 2026, in the Secretaries’ Cup at Audi Field in Washington, D.C. Matt Kaminsky/ZUMA Press Wire The Mariners face No. 25 Hampden-Sydney on the road Saturday at noon after a first-round bye. The USMMA returns to the playoffs for the first time since 1994, the academy’s only other berth. It’s a unique situation for midshipmen on the team who were slated to begin their term at sea — where they can be deployed anywhere around the globe — right after the regular season ended. Several players are spending their mornings on the academy’s flagship vessel, the Kings Pointer, as an interim solution while they wait for long-term stationing after the playoffs. They come back to land and practice in the evening, ready to work, Croall said. “Their ability to compartmentalize all of those things and be able to focus on what they need to focus on in the moment is really a pretty special quality that I think embodies our team. “We really don’t have many bad practices.” The Mariners have also been sailing to victory thanks to dual-threat junior quarterback Bubba Mustain, who averaged 100 rushing yards per game and threw for 16 touchdowns in nine weeks. “He’s really just a complete player with a team around him that’s fully bought in and able to make plays for him as well.”

item.title: King Rice opens up on absence from UNC basketball, emotional return | Exclusive
item.description: CHAPEL HILL — The emotions didn’t fully hit King Rice until he returned to the visiting locker room at the Smith Center following a 40-point loss to his alma mater. Rice, 57, certainly wasn’t pleased with Monmouth’s performance in an 85-45 defeat to North Carolina . But after nearly 500 games as the Hawks’ head coach over 16 seasons, he knows wins and losses come and go. What lingered was bigger than results. More than 40 years of memories and relationships came flooding back when Rice saw who was waiting for him after the game. MALONE'S PATH: Michael Malone goes from practice ejection to lifelong loyalty at Seton Hall Prep | Exclusive UNC BASKETBALL REUNION: The moment at UNC's basketball reunion that caught Michael Malone off guard Former UNC guard Kenny Smith was there. So were former Tar Heels assistant coaches Phil Ford and Dave Hanners. Dave Blaha, a former walk-on who often gave Rice rides home to upstate New York during their playing days, was there too. Rice hadn’t seen Blaha since the 1990s. “That’s when it got emotional for me,” Rice said during a 20-minute conversation with The Fayetteville Observer. “Because I didn’t play with Kenny. Obviously, Coach Ford coached me and helped me grow up a whole bunch. But then Coach Hanners came in there and said, ‘Listen to this guy. He cares about y’all, he loves y’all. I know he yells and uses curse words sometimes, but he’s trying to get y’all to do the right things. It’s all from the right place.’ ” It was a special moment because, as Rice mentioned, "those guys are Carolina men and they came to support me" at the Smith Center. “They know I don’t like losing like that. They know that crushed everything in my being, but you got to be a man, you got to stand up. This isn’t the first time I’ve gotten my butt kicked, it’s not going to be the last time I get my butt kicked," Rice said. “But, as a man, you got to stand up. Your friends are still there for you. Even though I didn’t play with those guys, they came to support and that’s where my kids can learn the most from. It’s bigger than basketball. Yeah, we got whupped (Monday), but it’s bigger than basketball and the experience was great for us. We’ll be better because of how that game went.” A loss is temporary. Family is forever. Why King Rice stayed away, eventually returned to UNC A four-year player for Dean Smith and the Tar Heels from 1987-91, Rice scored 861 points, dished out 629 assists and racked up 147 steals. He helped the program win two ACC Tournament championships and, as a captain in 1991, made the Final Four. item.title: Jared Lloyd named Missouri State football Media Player of the Year
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — The Missouri State Media Player of the Year award has returned. Linebacker Jared "Bird" Lloyd was named the 2026 Media Player of the Year on Tuesday, Nov. 24. The Media Player of the Year award had been given to the top Bears player from 1982-2017 and was revived in 2026. “This means a lot. I really appreciate you guys covering me and I’m very appreciative of you guys just getting my name out there more,” Lloyd said. “You guys reporting on me, doesn’t just help me. It helps my teammates, it helps the university and it helps the football program.” Missouri State football: Bears snag its top in-state recruit in the program's history Entering the final game of the season, Lloyd leads the nation with 127 total tackles. He also ranks No. 1 in tackles per game with 11.55. This is the best season by a Missouri State player since 2016, when Dylan Cole set the mark. This is the third-most tackles in a single Missouri State season since 2004. Lloyd also has two sacks, one forced fumble and three pass deflections. The Daytona Beach, Florida, native will finish his career with more than 275 tackles in his five seasons in Springfield. “Bird will go down in history as one of the most important players in Missouri State football history, shepherding this team into the FBS era. He has been one of the best tacklers in college football in 2026,” the News-Leader's Liam Keating said in a press release. “Instead of competing for individual accolades, he's always been a team-first player. This is what makes him a special player and worthy of the first media-given award in almost a decade.” Lloyd is the seventh linebacker to win the award. Ken Braden (1986), Matt Soraghan (’87), James Turnage (’88), DeLaun Fowler (’94-95), P.J. Jones (’01) and Cole (’15-16) were named winners. Missouri State: How star Kaemyn Bekemeier has mastered the NIL era "There's something satisfying about seeing the fruits of one's labor play out before your very eyes," Collingwood said. "Lloyd made a concerted effort to get leaner and quicker in the offseason, and it's translated into him being the country's most prolific tackler. Between his hard work, matter-of-fact disposition, productivity, and rare five-year allegiance to the same school, Lloyd is certainly deserving of this award." Missouri State (4-7, 3-4 CUSA) will host No. 21 Liberty (10-1, 7-0) at 1 p.m. for senior day on Saturday, Nov. 28. This will be Lloyd’s final game representing the Bears inside Plaster Stadium. Keating and the Daily Citizen’s Ryan Collingwood voted on the winner. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. item.title: KJ Duff reflects on Rutgers football legacy as his NFL decision looms
item.description: PISCATAWAY – All KJ Duff knew at the time was that he couldn’t finish the rest of the game. Rutgers football’s star wide receiver had reaggravated an injury during the Scarlet Knights ’ game against Michigan that he had suffered the week prior, but even as he walked off the SHI Stadium field the possibility he had played his last snap never crossed his mind. Then came the diagnosis of a high-ankle sprain, followed by surgery that would end his season four games too soon. “It definitely was frustrating,” Duff told USA TODAY-New Jersey this week. “All I really want to do is play football, and then that gets taken away.” Frustrating for Duff. Disappointing for the program. And perhaps more disappointing for a fanbase that, for three seasons, watched Duff develop into one of the best receivers in the program’s history, climbing lists in the record books, filling highlight reels with jaw-dropping catches and cementing a legacy that won’t soon be forgotten. Duff hasn’t officially announced his future – whether he’ll pursue the NFL or return to Rutgers for his final year of eligibility. But Duff is projected as a potential first-round draft pick. He’d become the first Rutgers player to hold that distinction since 2010. Coach Greg Schiano also said after a recent game that if Duff asked him, he’d advise him to pursue the NFL. If Duff makes that choice, Schiano made it clear he’ll miss having him in the program. The reasons why are clear. “I’ve told everybody that comes here, it was a lot of fun while it lasted because our hardest working player was our best player,” Schiano said. “That’s fun when you can point to him as an example. Especially in this era of so many newcomers, like, ‘Look what he’s doing, Try to do that.’” That work paid off. “It feels great to be recognized as that, but it's really about what you put into it,” Duff said. “I go with that mentality of, ‘I want to be great.’ I want to put myself in the best position to be successful.” Duff said his focus now is on getting healthy, which was off to a good start just more than two weeks after surgery. Duff said he was already doing some jogging and his doctors said he’s ahead of schedule in his recovery after initially saying he’d be able to resume football activities in January. “I don't want to rush anything and put myself in a bad position,” Duff said. KJ Duff stayed loyal to Rutgers football and developed into a star receiver Duff, who joined the program as the top overall recruit in New York for the 2024 recruiting class out of St. Anthony's High School on Long Island, in three seasons at Rutgers had 132 catches for 2,283 yards with 17 touchdowns. In eight games this season before getting hurt, Duff had 774 receiving yards on 45 catches with a season-high nine touchdowns. He had at least 100 receiving yards in four of those games. Xabi Alonso’s side went down 1-0 at the Stadium of Light before they were thrashed 4-1 at home by Leeds last weekend despite taking the lead. That was their fifth Premier League defeat in 11 games, leaving them eighth in the table and five points off the top four. Their opponents tonight have also had a tough start to the season with just two wins so far, which means they are outside the bottom three on goal difference only. One of those wins came against Manchester City a fortnight ago when Liam Delap scored twice to help his side to a shock 3-1 win and ended a five-game winless run. Both managers are under increasing pressure in their new roles, but it is Oliver Glasner, who is the favourite on betting sites to be the next manager to lose his job at 11/8, and he will know that the patience of Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis will only last so long. This will only be the 19th meeting in the Premier League, though and in those games the Blues have won just seven to Forest’s five, while the remaining six have been drawn. The strange statistic between these sides is that both have better away records, with Chelsea winning the last three matches at the City Ground, while Forest have won two and drawn two of the last four at Stamford Bridge. Last season, Josh Acheampong, Pedro Neto and Reece James were on target in a 3-0 win at Forest, before Malo Gusto was sent off three minutes before the end. item.description: One of the many things that makes Carlos Alcaraz so great is his constant willingness to improve. Time and time again, he has proven himself the best player in the world, having strolled to major titles or beaten his rivals with minimal fuss. Normally, that could encourage complacency, and he would have been forgiven for occasionally succumbing to that notion. However, that has yet to happen. Every time it feels like the 23-year-old simply cannot get any better, he manages it, with his current run of form no different. Carlos Alcaraz spent nearly five months sidelined due to injury this year, but even that has not prevented him from improving a key area of his game, which has now been compared to one of the sport’s greatest-ever players. Carlos Alcaraz discusses his changes to his serve Alcaraz’s serve has been a much-discussed topic for years now. After all, if a weakness had to be selected in the Spaniard’s game, this used to be it, with it more than capable, but far from a lethal weapon. Photo by Darren Carroll/USTA via Getty Images Then, last year, he served his way to US Open glory once again, reaching the final without dropping a set and getting broken just three times en route to the title. Even that was not enough, with Alcaraz reportedly having made further tweaks to this all-important shot. According to Marca , the latest changes are inspired by Pete Sampras, one of the greatest servers in tennis history, with particular focus on his raised foot movement during the motion. Samu Lopez, his coach, added: “We were looking for him to have more balance at the beginning of the movement, and that would help him to be more fluid and that he could push himself upwards.” Then, at a Davis Cup press conference earlier this week, Alcaraz directly addressed these changes, admitting: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. The tighter you play to the lines, the better your chances of getting into an attacking position or even winning the point. 🎙️Carlos on his serve improvements: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. It’s something we’ve improved and put a lot of focus on. “Since the US Open, this is the hardest I’ve worked on my serve. Accuracy was a big part of it, and we’ve worked on it more because I’m not very tall and can’t serve like some other players.” Earlier this year, Alcaraz’s serve was accused of ‘not doing enough damage’ . It’s incredible how he has managed to combat those complaints despite spending so long out injured with a wrist injury.

While expectations were modest compared with those surrounding Lewandowski, Jesus is beginning to show why Barcelona brought him to the club. His goalscoring return has been particularly impressive considering he has made only 11 appearances and had not completed a full match before the Champions League fixture against Sabah in Baku. Gabriel Jesus scores whenever Flick starts him One of the most striking aspects of Jesus’ Barcelona career so far is his record when selected from the beginning. Gabriel Jesus has scored five goals in very limited time for Barcelona. It was not a spectacular finish, but it still showed the instinctive positioning that has become a feature of his performances. Barcelona have discovered a natural finisher Jesus, who signed from Arsenal, has already shown different ways of scoring during his short Barcelona spell, having demonstrated quality in the air, the ability to finish with either foot, a powerful strike and composure when opportunities arrive inside the box. item.title: Real Madrid forward knows he is more likely to win the Ballon d’Or as a number nine
item.description: Real Madrid forward knows he is more likely to win the Ballon d’Or as a number nine As we near the halfway point of the season, it is safe to say that Kylian Mbappe has emerged as one of the best performers in Europe. The Frenchman has continued his goalscoring exploits at Santiago Bernabeu, having racked up as many as 19 goals across all competitions. Mbappe has looked quite fit in doing so as well, as he has played in every single one of Real Madrid’s matches so far, leading the club to believe that the player is at the peak of his physical performance. Mbappe’s bid to win Ballon d’Or Mbappe has embraced the number nine role at Real Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Given the sheer productivity Mbappe has provided to the table at Real Madrid this season, it goes without saying that he will once again be one of the candidates to win the Ballon d’Or next year. Keeping that in mind, El Chiringuito has recently claimed that Mbappe himself is aware of the fact that he has more chances of winning the Ballon d’Or if he continues to operate as a number nine. This comes against the backdrop of earlier allegations against Mbappe that he enjoys operating more as a left-winger. In the months since, Mbappe has now fully embraced the role of a number nine, and this has been quite evident in his performances this season. Although the Frenchman still has the tendency to drift out wide, he has done so far less frequently in recent weeks and his overall combination play with other attackers has improved tenfold. Real Madrid, as a result, have dominated their opponents. Can Mbappe win the Ballon d’Or? Mbappe finished second in the 2026 Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Mbappe’s numbers so far this season make it obvious that he will be one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d’Or next year. However, the Frenchman’s fate will once again depend on whether or not Real Madrid can secure any silverware this season. Los Blancos have not won a single major trophy in two seasons, so breaking that rut could go a long way in boosting Mbappe’s chances of winning his first Ballon d’Or. Fortunately, with Jose Mourinho, Real Madrid now have a seasoned coach who has shown exceptional decision-making skills and has the technical know-how in competitions such as the Champions League. Mbappe, to that end, will play an integral part of Mourinho’s war machine as they look to break Real Madrid’s trophy rut during the second half of the campaign.

item.title: Cam Smith reacts to shooting 64 in Australia despite hitting ‘the worst shot’ he has ever hit as a pro
item.description: Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images Cam Smith vaulted himself back into contention at the Australian PGA Championship on Friday. Smith shot a superb round of 64, one that even featured a bogey. The 33-year-old Australian carded seven birdies and an eagle during his second round at The Lakes on Friday. Cam Smith is now sitting just four shots adrift of the leader, Nicolai von Dellingshausen, with 36 holes left to play. Smith is looking to win his fourth Australian PGA Championship this week, and if he carries on playing like he did on Friday across the weekend, he will have a great chance to do just that. Cam Smith reacts to shooting 64 at the Australian PGA Smith wasn’t entirely happy with his opening round in Australia on Thursday, so he would have been delighted to see such drastic improvements on day two. The former LIV Golf star spoke to reporters after shooting a second-round 64 and responded when asked to give his verdict on his current form. “Yeah, I think so, it’s definitely going to be a different year. I’m excited. I haven’t done the European stuff before, and just starting at home is pretty special,” Smith said. “I got in a bit of a groove and rhythm today, which is what we’ve been looking for. We’ve been searching for that and it finally kind of all came together today.” However, not everything went swimmingly for Smith. The 2022 Open champion hit what he described as probably the worst shot he has ever hit as a professional on the par-three 15th hole. However, after leaving himself a full wedge shot into the green, he holed a 25-foot putt to salvage his par. “That might have been the worst shot I’ve ever hit as a professional,” said Smith. “It wasn’t a shank, but it was close. It definitely kind of kept the momentum going, for sure.” Cam Smith will be hoping to avoid any more card-wrecking shots like the one he hit on the 15th hole on Friday. If he manages to post two rounds in the 60s over the weekend, he may well have a chance of winning the fourth Australian PGA Championship of his career.

item.title: Bournemouth equal Nuremberg’s European record
item.description: Bournemouth equal Nuremberg’s European record Bournemouth are already dreaming on European glory under Marco Rose, and rightly so. After going 1-0 down against Celta Vigo in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday night, having a man sent off and then scoring two goals, the Cherries’ 2-1 victory is their fifth straight win in their maiden European competition. With five wins from five and maximum points, Bournemouth became the first English team, and only the third in history, to win their first five European matches. Only Nuremberg (1961/62) and Ararat Yerevan (1972/73) are the only other teams to record such a feat. It was also their tenth straight victory across all competitions – a record matched only by Real Madrid. Speaking to the BBC Sport after Bournemouth’s latest victory, Rose, formerly of Borussia Mönchengladbach, Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig, said: “Dreaming is always allowed. item.title: Eastleigh to keep Hill, Bristow & Bartram in charge
item.description: Richard Hill is in his fourth spell in charge of Eastleigh, having guided them to promotion to the National League in 2014 [Shutterstock] Eastleigh have confirmed that Richard Hill, Jason Bristow and Vince Bartram will continue to oversee first-team affairs for the foreseeable future. The trio have been in charge of the side on an interim basis since Matt Gray was sacked earlier this month. Former manager Hill had conducted post-match media affairs after Eastleigh's past two games - a 3-1 win at Tamworth and a 3-1 home loss to Yeovil Town. The club had won just one of their final eight matches under Gray and are currently 18th in the National League. The news comes days after owner Stewart Donald confirmed to fans he will leave the club at the end of the season. "Given the ongoing uncertainty surrounding the club's ownership, the board believes it is right to manage the first team within our existing resources," a statement released by Eastleigh read. "Our priority remains securing our place in the National League. "We also want to put together a strong run in the FA Trophy and carry that momentum into our league performances." The club has also confirmed Gray's assistant Jason Goodliffe has left the Spitfires by mutual consent.

item.title: Why Cambridgeshire derby could be season-defining
item.description: Robbie Savage's Peterborough United will seek to defend a long unbeaten home record in the Cambridgeshire derby when Neil Harris's U's visit London Road [Getty Images] History, tradition, bragging rights. Local derbies are always special, but none more so than when they have the ability to shape the narrative of a season. This much is true of Saturday's Cambridgeshire derby (12:30 GMT). Robbie Savage's Peterborough United welcome Neil Harris' Cambridge United to London Road with both at something of a crossroads. At stake for Posh? Their League One status. Despite an impressive win at Plymouth Argyle last time out, they remain 22nd in the table and need results to avoid a battle against the drop being the defining theme of their season. As for the U's, the derby presents an opportunity to regain momentum. After October's 2-1 win at Barnsley they were one point off top spot, but failure to pick up three points in any of their five league games since leaves them caught between play-off contention and mid-table drift. 'It's all about winning' The derby also carries the weight of recent history, with the emotional baggage greater for the U's. They have lost each of their past seven away league games against Peterborough, losing those matches by a combined 20-3 scoreline. Indeed, they have not won at London Road since an FA Cup tie in 1994-95, while their wait for a league win at their rivals' home extends to 1990. Savage, appointed last month, said his side were well aware of their responsibility for continuing that record. "We don't want to be the group that loses to Cambridge at home, first time in 30 years I think it would be," he said. "We don't want to be that group. We want to put three, four, five past them and win the game. Even if it's 1-0, it doesn't matter. "It's all about winning, don't care we win, just win the game." The victory at Plymouth ended a four-game wait for a win, and Savage said the onus was on his side to back it up on derby day. If they do, they know they will have secured successive league victories for the first time since February. "This game is at the top of the mountain," he said. "No doubt about it. The players will be up for it, we've shown them videos of the previous games, we've got fans sending messages. "We're doing everything we can to make them realise how big this game is. It's not another game, it's the derby. A great game. "Neil knows what it means. We're two passionate managers. He's done far better than me as a manager so far, so hats off to him. But we both want to win. "They will bring 1,600 fans and we need to show Cambridge that we want to county to be blue." While this derby is new territory for Savage, Harris comes armed with the memory of defeat in his only previous taste of the tie in a season than ultimately ended with relegation for the U's. item.title: Gasly amused by Verstappen and Russell feud: 'I'm just eating my popcorn'
item.description: Pierre Gasly has weighed in on the latest chapter of the bitter rivalry between Max Verstappen and George Russell , admitting that he is thoroughly enjoying watching the drama unfold from the sidelines. Tensions between Verstappen and Russell resurfaced during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend following an on-track altercation in the third and final free practice session, during which the pair made contact. The incident reignited a rivalry that reached boiling point at the end of the 2024 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, when the two drivers publicly traded accusations following a controversial qualifying incident in Lusail. Verstappen added further fuel to the fire following his victory in Las Vegas, claiming that Russell was "so far below my level" and remarking that "karma is a bi**h" following the Mercedes driver's difficult evening. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Russell was subsequently given the opportunity to respond to the Dutchman's remarks ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, describing the situation as unnecessary. The Mercedes driver stood by his criticism of Verstappen following their practice clash but insisted that he had no intention of prolonging their feud, acknowledging that he might have been too open when speaking to the media. Verstappen, meanwhile, refused to be drawn into another exchange of words with his rival during his media commitments in Qatar, insisting that everything that needed to be said off track had already been said. Gasly enjoys watching Verstappen and Russell's rivalry unfold The ongoing feud has also attracted the attention of several other drivers on the grid, including Gasly, who briefly partnered Verstappen at Red Bull in 2019 and has known both drivers since childhood. The Alpine driver admitted that he was enjoying the spectacle, suggesting that neither the altercation in Las Vegas nor the subsequent war of words came as a surprise to him: "Not the first time, not the last time these two are going to go at it. From my side I'm just sitting and eating my popcorn laughing about it." Gasly also offered an insight into how he approaches disagreements with his former teammate, explaining that he prefers to address any issues directly with the Dutchman. "I think it was best with Max just to tell him right up in his face! He's someone that just takes anything," the Frenchman told Sky Sports. "You can have opinions, etcetera. item.title: Australia's sandpapergate probe to also include 2017-18 Ashes
item.description: Australia won the 2017-18 Ashes series against England 4-0 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England. The terms of reference for the independent forum have been published and the scope will include "ball-management practices in the Australian men's team during the 2017–18 season", which includes the Ashes series Australia won 4-0. Also included are all four Tests of the subsequent South Africa tour and the investigation which followed when the ball-tampering scandal emerged. Cricket Australia has pledged to publish the full independent report and recommendations within 30 days of receiving them. All those involved in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa will be invited to speak to the independent forum, though none will have to do so and no retrospective sanctions will be handed out. The scandal was reignited by the release of former batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography. In it, Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about ball-tampering in the third Test of their series against South Africa in Cape Town. The four frontline bowlers in that 2018 team - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and current Test captain Pat Cummins - have always denied knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball. Cummins has called Khawaja's recollection of events "nonsense". However, former team-mates David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of three players who were banned for their part in the scandal, alongside Steve Smith - have backed Khawaja's version of events. "All participants in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa, including players and support staff, will be invited to take part in the Independent Forum, as will CA management and directors at that time," Cricket Australia said. "While all involved will be encouraged to participate, there will be no compulsion to do so. All materials supplied will be treated as confidential unless otherwise stated by the participant and no sanctions will be retrospectively applied. "Participants can choose to attend the Independent Forum in person, online and/or provide information via written accounts or through relevant documents and materials." The forum will be open for six weeks. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA Board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," CA chair David Boon said. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. "This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn. item.title: ‘I nearly had a heart attack!’ - Thomas Frank celebrates first Crystal Palace win after dramatic Europa League comeback against Real Sociedad
item.description: FBL-EUR-C3-CRYSTAL PALACE-REAL SOCIEDAD - AFP Thomas Frank has tasted his first victory as Crystal Palace manager, but the Danish coach admitted the frantic closing stages of their 2-1 win over Real Sociedad left him fearing for his health. The Eagles came from behind at Selhurst Park to secure a vital Europa League result that could act as a catalyst for their season. Late goals and red card spark Selhurst Park turnaround Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr fired Real Sociedad ahead in the 66th minute of Frank's first home match, only for Jon Martin's second yellow card six minutes later to hand Palace a numerical advantage. Jean-Philippe Mateta converted from the penalty spot before Dwight McNeil poked home from fellow substitute Jorgen Strand Larsen's overhead kick. Unai Marrero saved Yeremy Pino's spot-kick, leaving goalkeeper Dean Henderson to make the last of his six stops against Orri Oskarsson late on. Frank hails brave attacking gamble after nervy finish Reflecting on bouncing back from Saturday's debut defeat to Coventry, Frank praised his squad's response to falling behind . “I think first and foremost to get it over the line, and [it was] an extremely important win for various reasons,” he said. “One, of course, confidence, and it relates to belief against an extremely good team. I think the first half we were compact and very disciplined in many ways. We missed the high-pressure situations we had, and I think we struggled to keep the ball well enough. “Second half I felt we were much better in the high pressure, and I felt we kept the ball much better. I actually felt we got a bit more momentum in the second half but then, out of the blue, they scored the 1-0 goal. But what I really like is the belief from the players, what they showed, and that we are threatening on set-pieces, we cannot underestimate that.” Frank also credited his bold substitutions once Real Sociedad went down to 10 men. “We know in football one moment can change the game,” he continued. “The penalty and the red card changed the game, then we still needed to score. To win still is important and we went brave, we went with the offensive substitutions and kept two strikers on the pitch, and that paid off. And then I think we were all close to getting a heart attack in the last five minutes.” European play-off boost offers hope amid relegation fight While Premier League survival remains the priority for the bottom-placed Eagles, Thursday's victory lifted them into the Europa League play-off spots, four places outside the top eight after five games. “I think we want to aim high,” the former Tottenham boss replied when asked about his continental ambitions. “We are ambitious for this tournament, and that’s why the win was so important.” Frank also agreed the comeback could prove a major turning point for his squad's morale. “That’s why it’s so important to keep doing the right things, keep believing, and keep going,” he said. item.description: €50m Uruguay Star Wants Manchester United Move Manchester United Tracking Maxi Araújo as January Left-Back Question Grows Manchester United have spent months tracking Maxi Araújo, and according to Sport Witness , their interest remains active after seeing him first-hand in the 2-2 draw with Sporting. The key detail is simple enough. The player wants the move, United like the player, and the only real obstacle looks like the fee. Sport Witness report that a source close to the situation says the Uruguay international is “very open to joining the Premier League side”. That matters. In transfer talks, willingness from the player often does a lot of the heavy lifting. It does not close a deal, but it changes the temperature. Maxi Araújo Interest Looks Genuine This is not one of those stories built on one scout in the stands and a lot of noise. United have “closely followed Maxi Araújo for months”, and they used the Lisbon trip to take another proper look. Sport Witness add there is “mutual appreciation”, which usually means the groundwork has already been done quietly. Araújo also gave them something tangible on the pitch. He played the full 90 minutes against United and assisted Luis Suárez for Sporting’s opener in the 33rd minute. Over the season, he has made 15 appearances and was making his 14th start. Availability matters, and so does output. Photo IMAGO January Transfer Fee Remains Central Issue The numbers are clear. Araújo signed a new Sporting deal until 2030 in August, and that contract includes an €80m release clause. He is also on what Sport Witness describe as a “top salary at Sporting”. So nobody should expect a bargain. That said, the report adds that “€50-60m should be enough to take the player in January”. In modern terms, that is the real valuation point, not the clause. The problem for United is straightforward. The same source believes they are “unlikely to invest that amount of money on a fullback in January”. That sounds believable. Manchester United Left-Back Need Is Obvious United’s need at left-back is hardly a secret. Luke Shaw has again missed time with injury, while Harry Amass remains more of a developing option than a guaranteed solution. Contractually, there is no immediate pressure. Chiesa is tied to Liverpool until June 2028, which gives the club control and should help protect value. That could influence the structure of any deal, particularly if interested clubs in Italy push for favourable loan terms rather than a full transfer. item.title: Virgil van Dijk praises ‘outstanding’ Liverpool teammates after Club Brugge win
item.description: Virgil van Dijk praises ‘outstanding’ Liverpool teammates after Club Brugge win Liverpool 3-0 Club Brugge: Van Dijk Praises Champions League Response Liverpool did what good sides are supposed to do after a bad European result. They went away from home, kept control, took their chances and left with a clean 3-0 win over Club Brugge in the Champions League. After the frustrating defeat to Fenerbahce, when Liverpool had led twice and still came away empty-handed, there was a need for a proper response. They got one in Belgium. Alexander Isak scored twice, Florian Wirtz added the third, and the game was effectively a demonstration of efficiency. Photo IMAGO Van Dijk Sees Right Reaction Virgil van Dijk started on the bench, which remains an unusual sight in any major Liverpool fixture, and came on for the final 15 minutes. Even without starting, his influence was obvious. He said: “I am in the game, encouraging and trying to do the type of things I usually do when I’m playing.” He added: “Off the pitch, in the warm-up, in the dressing room, I try to do all the same things but obviously you have a bit less influence.” That is the point with senior players. If they are switched on, they matter whether they play 90 minutes or 15. Alexander Isak And Florian Wirtz Deliver Club Brugge arrived in form and posed a tactical problem with aggressive man-marking all over the pitch. Liverpool handled it well. They moved the ball cleanly, punished openings and never let the game drift into chaos. Van Dijk summed it up plainly: “Overall it was a very good performance against a team who have been in form. They can be tricky to play against as they go with man-marking all over the pitch. “But our guys were so clinical, so good in the way we kept the ball. Defensively, we were solid as well. A great night.” Van Dijk reserved special praise for the younger players and the defence, saying: “The whole back line did so good, Trey [Nyoni] as well in front of them. The whole team were outstanding.” That is the real takeaway. Liverpool did not overcomplicate the evening. They corrected the mistakes of the Fenerbahce loss, stayed compact, stayed sharp and got the result they needed. As Van Dijk put it: “It was important to show a reaction away after what happened away to Fenerbahce. That was a disappointing night for us. But it’s about how you deal with what’s coming next and we’ve done that pretty well.”

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville.
